content:
Lena Fischer: digging into today’s mixed-workload runs (prefill/decode 35/65, conc=32). Microbench says FP8 attention is a clear win, but e2e improvements are getting eaten. I suspect scheduler knobs (batching window + backpressure) are masking the kernel gains. Anyone have time to sanity check tradeoffs / recommend defaults for the sprint?

Omar El-Sayed: +1. the shape wins show up when we actually form decent decode microbatches. in “realistic” traffic we’re bursting, then we start prefill-heavy, then decode trickles → scheduler keeps draining small batches to protect TTFT.

Sofia Ivanova: what knobs are you thinking specifically? we’ve got:
- `scheduler.max_batching_delay_us` (global)
- `scheduler.decode_max_microbatch_tokens`
- `scheduler.prefill_max_microbatch_tokens`
- backpressure: `scheduler.queue_depth_soft_limit` + `scheduler.queue_depth_hard_limit`
- `scheduler.prefill_priority_boost`

Lena Fischer: yep. right now in the harness config for suite-v3 we’re using:
- max_batching_delay_us=250
- decode_max_microbatch_tokens=4096
- prefill_max_microbatch_tokens=2048
- queue_depth_soft=2, hard=4

When I bump delay to 800us, tokens/s jumps, but TTFT p95 gets ugly on shorter prompts.

Marcus Reed: I’m looking at the new scheduler histograms from PR-19855 (queue depth + prefill/decode split). At delay=250us we’re almost always at `decode_batch_size=1` or `2` for the long-tail of decode. That basically turns the FP8 kernel win into “meh” because launch overhead dominates.

Julian Moore: attaching quick numbers from my run (H100, model=top-hosted-#2, workload=mix-35/65, prompt p50=512/p95=2k, gen=256):
- baseline kernels, delay=250us: TTFT p50=310ms / p95=510ms, TPOT p50=16.8ms / p95=24.1ms, throughput=12.9 tok/s/user
- FP8 kernels, delay=250us: TTFT p50=315ms / p95=520ms, TPOT p50=15.9ms / p95=23.6ms, throughput=13.2 tok/s/user
- FP8 kernels, delay=700us: TTFT p50=345ms / p95=640ms, TPOT p50=12.8ms / p95=18.9ms, throughput=15.1 tok/s/user

So: TPOT/throughput improves a lot, TTFT p95 regresses.

Hiro Tanaka: this matches what we saw in the FP8 attention thread. kernel is faster, but scheduler is trading it away for TTFT. question is what do we want for hosted defaults? and can we make the batching delay adaptive instead of static.

Noah Patel: +1 on “adaptive”. static delay makes the benchmark “choose your poison”. in prod we typically want:
- low-ish TTFT at low/moderate load
- maximize throughput only once queue depth indicates sustained load

We can do something like:
- if queue depth <= 1: delay=~150-250us
- if queue depth >= 2: ramp to 500-800us
- cap delay when we detect prefill backlog

(need to confirm we can implement cleanly without making perf canary noisy)

Sofia Ivanova: we already have the pieces to do that, but we’ve historically avoided because it’s easy to create oscillations. the backpressure knobs matter a ton here.

Omar El-Sayed: also: prefill/decode interleaving policy. if we “protect TTFT” too aggressively, decode never batches and TPOT suffers. if we let decode batch, TTFT suffers because prefills wait.

Rina Kobayashi: from harness side: we can easily parameter sweep `max_batching_delay_us` + queue depth limits and upload a 2D matrix. but we need to define acceptance thresholds (variance + “don’t regress TTFT p95 > X”). otherwise we’ll bikeshed.

Marcus Reed: I think the right framing is:
1) kernel wins mainly reduce per-token compute (decode dominant)
2) scheduler decides whether we realize it via batch formation
3) on mixed workloads, TTFT p95 is set by how long prefill waits behind decode batching

So we need to explicitly decide the TTFT vs TPOT trade.

Allison Grant: from the canary POV, we can monitor both TTFT and TPOT separately (tagged by kernel mode + model + region). But if we ship an “adaptive delay” we need stable baselines. Otherwise we’ll get a ton of false positives like the last time we tweaked batching windows.

Rafael Mendes: +1. if the policy depends on instantaneous queue depth, your metrics shift with traffic patterns. canary will think it’s a regression when it’s just different load mix. we need the policy to be simple + easy to reason about, or we define canary cohorts that match load conditions.

Lena Fischer: ok, what if we keep policy simple for sprint:
- keep `max_batching_delay_us` at 250us as default
- add “high load mode” behind flag: if queue depth >= soft_limit for >N ms, temporarily allow delay up to 700us for decode-only batches
- ensure prefill never waits more than (say) 300us extra

This way TTFT stays protected for low load, but decode batching improves when we’re actually under pressure.

Sofia Ivanova: directionally good. but the “prefill never waits more than X” needs explicit implementation. easiest is a prefill priority boost that increases as prefill age increases.

Julian Moore: we can approximate with:
- maintain `prefill_age_us` per request
- when any prefill_age_us > threshold, force next step to run prefill batch regardless of decode queue

That avoids the pathological “decode always wins” scenario.

Hiro Tanaka: also keep in mind the FP8 attention path has higher launch overhead in some shapes. if we create too many microbatches, we’ll look worse even if compute is faster. batching is extra important for FP8.

Noah Patel: another simpler knob: increase `decode_max_microbatch_tokens` a bit (or allow larger decode microbatches), but only if we’re not memory constrained. on H100 we have headroom; on A100 we might hit KV cache pressure.

Omar El-Sayed: careful: bigger decode microbatches can increase tail TPOT if we block on a big batch. we should watch p95 TPOT not just p50.

Marcus Reed: one thing we should stop doing is using *one* batching delay for both prefill and decode. prefill wants low delay, decode wants larger delay. can we split delay by stage?

Sofia Ivanova: yes, but it’s not wired today. it’s a bigger change. might be too risky for this sprint unless we keep it behind a flag.

Rina Kobayashi: harness can support it if you give me two config keys. but if runtime doesn’t support, no point.

Lena Fischer: can we converge on an experiment plan for tomorrow? I propose we run suite-v3 on H100 with FP8 kernels with these configs:
A) delay=150us, soft=2 hard=4
B) delay=250us, soft=2 hard=4 (current)
C) delay=500us, soft=2 hard=6
D) delay=700us, soft=3 hard=8
and for each, record TTFT/TPOT p50/p95 + throughput + queue depth distribution.

Allison Grant: works. please also tag runs with scheduler config hash so dashboards can slice it (we’ve been burned by “which config was this?”).

Julian Moore: yep, I can add `scheduler_config_id` to the benchmark metadata export if it’s not already there. (should be in PR-19880 artifacts, but I’ll double-check.)

Rafael Mendes: for canary readiness: please define what’s an acceptable TTFT p95 regression. SRE needs a number for auto-rollback.

Noah Patel: proposal for hosted: allow TTFT p95 regression up to 3% if TPOT p95 improves >= 8% and error rate unchanged. anything >5% TTFT p95 is a no-go by default; can be enabled per-model with product signoff.

Sofia Ivanova: that’s reasonable. caveat: TTFT variance is high on small sample sizes. maybe enforce minimum N and use a smoothed window.

Marcus Reed: also we should consider “time-to-first-token under streaming” vs raw TTFT. some configs create spikier TTFT but much better steady-state generation. need to align with what we publish.

Lena Fischer: cool. I’ll run the sweep + post results here and in the daily notes. Action items:
- (Lena) run H100 sweep A-D for 2 models (one long-context heavy)
- (Julian) verify scheduler_config_id is exported + queue depth histos in artifacts
- (Sofia/Omar) propose a simple adaptive/backpressure policy we can ship behind flag
- (Rafael/Allison) draft tentative canary thresholds for TTFT/TPOT tradeoffs

Hiro Tanaka: :thumbsup: and please include at least one A100 run for the best config so we don’t pick something that only works on H100.

Rina Kobayashi: :thumbsup: if you post artifact links, I’ll add them to the matrix sheet and annotate anomalies.

Rafael Mendes: thanks. also if any config causes TTFT spikes >10% in p95, please don’t push it to canary even behind flag without a heads up. we’ve got the incident bot hair-triggered right now.

Lena Fischer: noted. will keep it bench-only until we agree on thresholds.
